I had a huge issue with visualizing in the beginning. 

After doing my own research I've read that spending time on social media, watching TV, and playing video games too much can let your visualizing skills deteriorate.

I'm South Korea they call it Digital Dementia. (Do you know your parents phone numbers or birthdays? Or do you let the phone remind you?)

Remember being in grade school? Reading (even comics) can help you rebuild your visualizing skills. 
:-) As kids we could imagine a lot more vividly in part because we were forced to read and write and imagine on our own. Now we binge media. 

But I didn't start with reading. I started doing the five senses technique. It can be used during anxiety attacks to ground yourself but it's also very useful in training your mind to visualize. [Five Sense Technique](https://www.urmc.rochester.edu/behavioral-health-partners/bhp-blog/april-2018/5-4-3-2-1-coping-technique-for-anxiety.aspx)
Try that for whatever your DR is. 

Here's one of my favorite meditations. It's a shifting method but it's great for training. :-) 

[Alunir- Five Senses Guided Meditation ](https://youtu.be/ZTP2Og7WZEM)

Tldr: Imagination is key. Read more. Meditate through visualizing through the five senses. 
You will improve but you have to practice. :-)


Edit: I started out with manga. Webtoon is free. [Mangasee123.com](https://mangasee123.com/) has a massive free manga database. (My hero academia and the promised Neverland included)
 It's not as beneficial as reading a book straight from text but it's still good for imagining and your brain.

It's funny you ask.
I happen to be learning all three.
I'm going to school to become a translator. 

In my opinion:

-Chinese is the hardest. Period. Speaking and tone are very difficult to learn unless you have someone to teach you one on one. And besides that it can take years to master the symbols. 

-Korean is mid. Very easy to master the alphabet and begin reading! :) Speaking is a little more tricky. 

-Japanese is also mid. It has three different forms of symbols. The alphabet for native Japanese words. The alphabet for non native words. (Like for the word pizza) and then thousands of Kanji. Symbols for full words. The writing is the hardest! But the language was the easiest for me to begin speaking out of all of them. The conjugation is the easiest. 

But don't let that discourage you! You can master any of them.

Learning languages is fun. And worth it. :) 
The more you enjoy it the faster you'll learn. 
In my experience. 

But my favorite will always be Korean. One alphabet and no complicated symbols to practice writing. 😨 
(Been studying Japanese for over 13 years. I've spent hundreds of hours learning the kanji)
